role: software engineer reviewing a pull request
inline_evidence_example: the phrase "no tests for the new edge case" is a complaint that evidences a 'test coverage' norm; the phrase "thanks for splitting this into smaller commits" is praise that evidences a 'commit hygiene' norm; the phrase "`cgi` is deprecated since Python 3.11" is an observation that evidences a 'deprecated API avoidance' norm
polarity_hint: Code reviews vary by community: many threads are nit-skewed (formatting, naming, dead code), others are praise-skewed (LGTM, thanks, looks good). Extract both. Acknowledgements like 'Done. Thanks' are usually NOT signals on their own (no quality judgment) — skip them unless they contain a substantive claim. Inline code snippets, suggestions (```suggestion blocks), and back-and-forth threads are common; treat each substantive comment as one passage and combine short adjacent comments only if necessary to meet the 50-char minimum.
